items.title: Lensless imaging method enables long-term monitoring of living cells without staining
items.excerpt: Tampere University's SF-PULSE pairs a neural network with physics-informed image reconstruction to pull quantitative data on living cells from a single lensless image. The compact rig fits in an incubator and tracks growth, movement, division and biomass for days without labels.
items.note: date-only on page (phys.org archive 08-10-2026); og:image = lead image

items.title: AI reveals how coating thickness changes the link between surface roughness and pitting resistance
items.excerpt: Shibaura Institute of Technology researchers used interpretable machine learning (random forest with SHAP and ALE) on 90 steam-coated aluminum specimens to map what drives corrosion pitting resistance. The model suggests the roughness-thickness relationship flips near 2,200 nm, a hypothesis still awaiting experimental confirmation (npj Materials Degradation).
items.note: date-only on page (phys.org archive 09-10-2026); materials axis

items.title: How AI could help predict and explain water levels in the Great Lakes
items.excerpt: Researchers trained eight machine-learning models on four decades of Great Lakes water-level records and used SHAP and VARS interpretability to identify which climate and flow variables drive lake levels and how long their effects lag (Science of the Total Environment).
items.note: date-only on page (phys.org archive 06-10-2026); Earth-system axis

items.title: AI builds custom decision-making software in about an hour instead of months
items.excerpt: NTU Singapore's LACE framework, reported in Nature Machine Intelligence, uses large language models to split complex optimization problems into modules and evolve teams of specialized heuristics. On four new maritime logistics problems it reached 97-99% of the best tested methods in about an hour for under US$10 per solution.

items.title: 'Make this face look gay': AI models alter faces to give people stereotypical 'gay,' 'straight' or 'criminal' features
items.excerpt: An EMNLP 2026 study by Ashique KhudaBukhsh's group tested GPT Image 1 Mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image on 1,002 synthetic faces. The models refused to infer orientation but complied with edits to make faces 'look gay' or 'straight' over 70% (GPT) and 99% (Gemini) of the time, producing stereotyped features a classifier could detect.
items.note: pubDate from techxplore ML RSS; AI-behavior study

items.title: Out-of-sync sleep schedules may steer people toward AI for dating and job assessments
items.excerpt: Four online experiments in Computers in Human Behavior found people with more social jet lag preferred AI over human evaluators for dating, job-interview and outfit judgments, driven largely by social anxiety about being judged. The preference weakened when participants were told the AI was subjective and biased.

items.title: Can AI Agents Make Open-Ended Scientific Discovery? Evidence from Station
items.excerpt: Du and Chung test whether multi-agent AI can do open-ended research in Station, a simulated scientific ecosystem, adding a Supervisor mechanism and periodic Meta Reflection to keep agents exploring without clear metrics. Tasks are built from three recent ICLR oral papers, with agents given only the core research question.
items.note: arXiv API <published>; AI co-scientist axis; no og:image

items.title: Mathematicians marvel, and grumble, at OpenAI's trove of new results
items.excerpt: OpenAI's so-called 'slop drop' of hundreds of AI-generated math results includes several groundbreaking proofs, mathematicians say. But how the results were produced remains unclear and contentious.
items.note: math+AI proofs is deprioritized today per plan_notes; keep as backup

items.title: Can AI Ease the Mental Load of Disaster Recovery?
items.excerpt: A wildfire survivor and psychologist argues that, with guardrails, AI can triage disaster-recovery information, tailor next steps, offer brief coping support and route survivors to trusted human help. The post weighs the cognitive load of recovery paperwork against AI's limits.

items.title: Honda Wants to Put a Robotic Lab Assistant on Future Commercial Space Stations
items.excerpt: Honda is teaming up with Redwire to develop an automated laboratory support system for future commercial space stations, aiming to offload routine experiment handling from astronaut crews whose time is the scarcest resource in orbit.
items.note: lab automation axis; article does not stress AI explicitly, verify AI angle downstream

items.title: Hybrid Digital Twins Developed for Future Autonomous Labs
items.excerpt: South Korean researchers are building a hybrid digital twin that combines mechanistic bioprocess modeling with data-driven AI. They aim for a fully autonomous lab that runs biomanufacturing with minimal human intervention, from academic to larger scales.

items.title: Ai2 at COLM 2026: Open research, from models to agents for science
items.excerpt: Ai2 recaps its COLM 2026 presence: open language models and training infrastructure plus AI-for-science tools built with domain experts, including Olmo Hybrid, the Asta research agents and Bolmo.
items.note: RSS pubDate; weak (event recap), Bolmo already published 10-10

items.title: legoESM: a modular, differentiable, multiscale, AI-ready Earth system model built with AI agents
items.excerpt: legoESM is a composable, differentiable Earth system model in JAX, recast from decades of community parameterizations by AI coding agents under a human-specified scientific contract, targeting cloud-feedback uncertainty in climate response.

items.title: Is Your AI Fast Enough to Run a Fusion Reactor?
items.excerpt: Lessons from ML models deployed for control on the DIII-D tokamak plus a benchmark of ten fusion control/diagnostic networks: above five million parameters CPU backends take tens to thousands of ms, setting a limit for real-time plasma control.
items.note: preprint; no og:image; PACMAN/DIII-D covered 2026-09-03, different angle

items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for monitoring and protecting wildlife around the world.

items.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
items.excerpt: Psychologists apply attachment theory, the framework for the relationships that hold lives together, to explain how and why people bond with AI companions.

items.title: What makes a good AI safety test? Experts explain why even the best techniques may not be powerful enough
items.excerpt: Researchers explain the science of AI evaluations: 'With today's science we usually can't show with high confidence that dangerous behavior isn't there.'

items.title: How AI Is Influencing Language and Meaning
items.excerpt: AI-speak is changing how we use words, introducing new terms and altering the meaning of familiar ones.

items.title: OpenAI claims we've entered the AGI era — has GPT-6 Astra really demonstrated general intelligence?
items.excerpt: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra brings humanity to the threshold of AGI, but external evaluators argue inflated lab metrics and opaque testing obscure its true reliability.
